16                THE SECRETARY:   Legislative 

17   Resolution Number 1588, by Senator DeFrancisco, 

18   congratulating UConn Women's Basketball Player        

19   Breanna Stewart upon the occasion of being named 

20   the NCAA's Most Outstanding Player in the 2013 

21   Final Four Tournament.  

22                "WHEREAS, It is the sense of this 

23   Legislative Body to recognize those outstanding 

24   individuals in the State of New York who 

25   consistently strive for athletic and academic 


                                                                2877

 1   excellence through rigorous training and mental 

 2   and physical discipline; and 

 3                "WHEREAS, Attendant to such concern, 

 4   and in full accord with its long-standing 

 5   traditions, this Legislative Body is justly proud 

 6   to congratulate UConn Women's Basketball Player 

 7   Breanna Stewart upon the occasion of being named 

 8   the NCAA's Most Outstanding Player in the 2013 

 9   Final Four Tournament; and 

10                "WHEREAS, By scoring 23 points, 

11   capturing nine rebounds and providing three 

12   assists, Breanna Stewart, a forward, led the 

13   UConn Huskies to a 93-60 victory over the 

14   Louisville Cardinals in the national championship 

15   game of the NCAA Women's Basketball Tournament on 

16   April 10, 2013; and 

17                "WHEREAS, The special victory over 

18   the Louisville Cardinals secured the University 

19   of Connecticut's eighth NCAA Title; and 

20                "WHEREAS, Breanna Stewart and the 

21   UConn Huskies advanced to the national 

22   championship game after defeating Notre Dame 

23   83-65 in the national semifinal game; Breanna 

24   Stewart scored a career-high 29 points with four 

25   blocks during the game; and 


                                                                2878

 1                "WHEREAS, Breanna Stewart was 

 2   dominant in all five NCAA tournament games by 

 3   scoring a total of 104 points; and   

 4                "WHEREAS, For her superior efforts, 

 5   Breanna Stewart was named Most Outstanding Player 

 6   of the Women's Final Four" -- 

 7                (Interruption from the gallery.)

 8                THE SECRETARY:   -- "of the Women's 

 9   Final Four" --

10                ACTING PRESIDENT SAVINO:   

11   {Gaveling.}  Order.  Order.   

12                THE SECRETARY:   -- "just the fourth  

13   freshman in history, and the first since 1987, to 

14   earn the honor; and 

15                "WHEREAS, Breanna Stewart can now 

16   add the titles of 2013 Final Four Most 

17   Outstanding Player, 2013 NCAA Champion, and 2013 

18   NCAA Tournament Bridgeport Regional Most 

19   Outstanding Player to her long list of 

20   achievements, which include being named  

21   Gatorade's 2011-2012 National High School Player  

22   of the Year during her senior year at 

23   Cicero-North Syracuse High School; and 

24                "WHEREAS, Breanna Stewart continues 

25   to make her team, family and Central New York 


                                                                2879

 1   community proud by demonstrating outstanding 

 2   athleticism, exemplary leadership, and a strong 

 3   drive to win; now, therefore, be it 

 4                "RESOLVED, That this Legislative 

 5   Body pause in its deliberations to congratulate 

 6   UConn Women's Basketball Player Breanna Stewart  

 7   upon the occasion of being named the NCAA's Most 

 8   Outstanding Player in the 2013 Final Four 

 9   Tournament; and be it further 

10                "RESOLVED, That a copy of this 

11   resolution, suitably engrossed, be transmitted to 

12   Breanna Stewart."

13                ACTING PRESIDENT SAVINO:   Senator 

14   DeFrancisco on the resolution.

15                SENATOR DeFRANCISCO:   Thank you, 

16   Madam President.  

17                We wanted to provide some 

18   entertainment for our guests --

19                (Laughter.)

20                SENATOR DeFRANCISCO:   -- and we 

21   asked those people to come out here and throw 

22   some money on the floor and make absolute fools 

23   out of themselves.  

24                It got a laugh out of her.  

25   Unfortunately, it's not something that ought to 


                                                                2880

 1   be done.

 2                Thank you for recognizing me, 

 3   Madam President.  I am very proud to welcome 

 4   Breanna Stewart and her father, Brian Stewart, to 

 5   the chambers today.  

 6                Last year, if you recall, we brought 

 7   her here and honored her as the number-one high 

 8   school women's basketball player in the country.  

 9   And she was here with her team, who won the state 

10   championship.

11                This year, as a freshman, she was 

12   named in the semifinals of the Women's NCAA 

13   tournament, playing for Connecticut, the most 

14   outstanding player of the regional tournament, I 

15   should say.  She was named the Most Outstanding 

16   Player in the Final Four Tournament.  

17                And despite all the great 

18   ballplayers in the past, there was only four 

19   others that won this honor of Player of the Year 

20   in the tournament, Most Valuable Player, since 

21   the history of the game.  

22                She's got three more great years to 

23   look forward to at Connecticut, and her 

24   performance was outstanding.  Not only that, 

25   she's a wonderful young woman who handled herself 


                                                                2881

 1   with dignity when she was interviewed during the 

 2   course of those games, and she is a wonderful 

 3   person who has a fantastic academic record.

 4                And I told no one I would tell them 

 5   till I got on the floor, but she's from my 

 6   district.

 7                (Laughter.)

 8                SENATOR DeFRANCISCO:   But no one 

 9   could ever -- no one is surprised by that because 

10   we bring so many champions here.  

11                So Breanna, congratulations on your 

12   wonderful success.  Brian, as her father, and 

13   relay to her mother, congratulations on raising 

14   such a fine young woman.  And we wish both of you 

15   and your entire family the best of everything in 

16   the future.

17                ACTING PRESIDENT SAVINO:   Thank 

18   you, Senator DeFrancisco.

                                                                2882

 8   constituent, but she happens to be attending my 

 9   alma mater, the University of Connecticut.  So I 

10   congratulate not only her but also the UConn 

11   Huskies on their eighth national championship.  

12                Thank you.

14   you.

20                This is very, very exciting.  As you 

21   know, I'm a basketball fan.  And I was very proud 

22   to bring Jimmer Fredette a few years ago.

25   so ...


                                                                2883

 6                Congratulations.  You certainly are 

 7   a talented young woman, and we look forward to 

 8   many, many more successes as you go forward.  

 9   Thank you for being here.

21                SENATOR KRUEGER:   Thank you, 

22   Madam President.

23                I have debated this bill in the past 

24   with Senator Griffo, so I saw no reason to repeat 

25   the debate this year.  


                                                                2890

 1                But to highlight, again, this is a 

 2   child health and safety concern.  And in fact the 

 3   New York State Department of Health cautions that 

 4   the average of 2,250 children 19 years of age or 

 5   less are taken to the hospital every year in 

 6   New York because of ATV-related injuries.  This 

 7   averages out to six children a day.  And that 

 8   particularly given the desire to prevent harm to 

 9   children, the fact is that one-third of those 

10   children are hospitalized with traumatic brain 

11   injury.  

12                There are many members of this house 

13   who may not share my concerns about ATV driving 

14   and young children, but there are many who are 

15   concerned about traumatic brain injury and the 

16   discoveries they are making each day about the 

17   impact for the rest of a young person's life from 

18   such injuries.

19                I urge that this state not move to 

20   the higher-class weights of ATVs and never allow 

21   children to be driving them.

22                Thank you, Madam President.  I'll be 

23   voting no.
